To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
nitric oxide promotes cancer stem cell formation by disrupting an Oct 4:caveolin 1 complex.

nitric oxide (NO), a small gaseous signaling molecule, promotes cancer cell dediffentiation by disrupting an OCT4:Caveolin-1 (cav-1) complex, a mechanism that leads to the formation of cancer stem cells.

NO promotes the stem cell regulatory activity of the transcription factor Oct4 through a novel mechanism that involves disruption of a molecular complex between Oct4 and a scaffolding protein, Cav-1, and that NO promotes Akt-dependent Cav-1 phosphorylation, which destabilizes the Oct4:Cav-1 complex.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of new molecular targets for the design of novel therapeutics to fight cancer stem cells (CSPs), which are believed to be responsible for cancer recurrence and metastasis.
the identification of the molecular mechanisms by which the CSC regulatory protein Oct4 is regulated in cancer cells, with a focus on the role of nitric oxide.
the mechanisms of cancer stem cells, which are a subpopulation of tumor cells that are responsible for cancer progression, metastasis and resistance to therapy.
